correctness.rationale: Independent reduction of the prime swapping orbit: in midpoint/difference coordinates use the cycle labels (m±p,q±r) and parameter e=p/r. The difference equations give m=1/2+b/(1−e²), q=−be/(1−e²). Put s=r² and s0=(b+1)/2. The mean one-step determinant divided by 4 is m²−bm−q²+(e²−1)s; the half-difference divided by 4 is r[(2m−b)e−2q]. At e=0 these are −1/4 and 0. Imposing their squared difference equal to 1/16 gives s=s0+[b+s0+2s0(3b+1)²]e²+O(e⁴). Inserting this in a=m+m²+e²s+q²+s and δ=(1−2(b−m))q+2es gives coefficient (b+1)(3b+1)(3b+2) in e² and δ=(1−b)e+O(e³). This verifies the curvature, signs, and both zero couplings. The base trace is 4b²−2 and determinant 1, so the second iterate lacks multiplier +1 for fixed −1<b<0; the analytic cycle continuation remains prime. Along δ=0 the determinant slope is 8, giving the analytic threshold and the claimed attracting-to-repelling spectral crossing. The exchange symmetry gives the even remainder. The check does not assume a nonresonant normal form or assert uniformity near the endpoints.
